facts.text: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing runs a model of the control logic against a model of the machine and its surroundings, without real software or hardware.
facts.quote: Model-in-the-loop testing runs a model of the control logic against a model of the machine and its surroundings, with no real software or hardware yet.

facts.text: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing runs a decision-logic block diagram in a modeling tool against a simple machine model before code is written for the real controller, allowing designers to check whether the rules behave sensibly before anything is built.
facts.quote: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) runs that diagram in the same tool against a simple machine model, so the designers can see whether the rules behave sensibly long before anything is built.

facts.text: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing is the cheapest and earliest rung of the testing ladder.
facts.quote: It is the cheapest and earliest rung of the ladder.

facts.text: Model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop testing serve the volume end of the validation pipeline, with thousands of runs per night on cloud or on-premise compute.
facts.quote: "model-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop for volume (thousands of runs per night on cloud or on-premise compute)" [Chapter 9]

facts.text: The middle-cost model-based tool chain supports model-in-the-loop (MIL), software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing from the same models.
facts.quote: the model-based tool chain it describes at the middle cost level supports MIL, SIL and HIL from the same models [Chapter 11]

facts.text: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing provides no knowledge about sensors or real timing.
facts.quote: Nothing about sensors or real timing can be learned here

facts.text: Model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing can catch logical mistakes, such as a warning zone that never triggers when the machine is articulated, while a fix still costs minutes.
facts.quote: the value is in catching logical mistakes, such as a warning zone that never triggers when the machine is articulated, while a fix costs minutes.

facts.text: The decision logic of a warn-then-brake function is far simpler than an automated-driving planner.
facts.quote: The decision logic of a warn-then-brake function is far simpler than an automated-driving planner [Chapter 7]

facts.text: Much of the warn-then-brake decision logic can be designed and checked at model-in-the-loop (MIL) level in late 2026, before the sensor is chosen, because that logic is far simpler than an automated-driving planner.
facts.quote: so much of it can be designed and checked at MIL level in late 2026, before the sensor is chosen.
